To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human genome contains 3.3 billion bases of DNA, 20,000 genes, and a total of 1.5 million protein coding sequences (exons).

(a) the expression of a subset of genes, including many that are associated with the development of cancer, is controlled by a single transcriptional regulatory network that is conserved in human and mouse, and (b) the network is regulated by the same set of transcription factors, which are also conserved in human, mouse, and zebrafish.

(i) the expression of the human genome in normal tissues is much more complex than previously assumed, with a large fraction of genes being expressed at low levels and with a large fraction having a complex expression profile, (ii) the human genome is highly dynamic in normal tissues, and (iii) the expression of many genes is highly tissue specific.
